s1.syndrome_frame: Tooth pain with abnormal root canal morphology and periapical radiolucency
salient_findings: Spontaneous dull pain during root canal therapy
Tender response to percussion
No response to cold or electric pulp tests
Periapical radiolucency at apex of DB root
C-shaped canal morphology in P root
key_facts: Patient is a 26-year-old female
Referred for root canal retreatment of tooth #17
Tooth sealed with temporary filling material
Negative medical history
Radiopaque filling material visible in coronal third of canal
Two different canal orifices in coronal third of P canal
Canals joined to form C-shaped ribbon-like pattern in middle third
Two P canals joined to one foramen in apical part

shortlist.label: Chronic Apical Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: Tooth tender to percussion and periapical radiolucency present

shortlist.label: C-Shaped Canal Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: CBCT findings revealed C-shaped canal morphology in P root

shortlist.label: Missed Canal
shortlist.why_kept: Two different canal orifices in coronal third of P canal and canals joined to form C-shaped ribbon-like pattern

shortlist.label: Root Canal Treatment Failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient referred for root canal retreatment due to spontaneous dull pain

shortlist.label: Periapical Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Periapical radiolucency present at apex of DB root

raw.rationale: The presence of two different canal orifices in the coronal third of the P canal and the C-shaped canal morphology, which was not fully addressed in the initial root canal treatment, suggests that a canal was missed, leading to the need for retreatment.

rejected.label: Chronic Apical Periodontitis
rejected.why: While the patient presents with periapical radiolucency, the primary issue seems to be related to the incomplete treatment of the root canal system rather than a chronic inflammatory condition.

rejected.label: C-Shaped Canal Syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has a C-shaped canal, this is more of an anatomical description rather than a diagnosis for the current clinical problem.

rejected.label: Root Canal Treatment Failure
rejected.why: This is a broader category that encompasses the current situation but does not specifically address the likely cause of the failure, which is the missed canal.

rejected.label: Periapical Cyst
rejected.why: There is no specific indication of a cystic structure in the provided information; the periapical radiolucency could be due to several reasons, including but not limited to, a missed canal.
